caption: Ethiopia news today: what is drought doing to Ethiopia's crops? Late June-September rains linked to El Niño destroyed crops on 250,035 hectares, an IFRC report says. More than 3.5 million people are affected in 101 districts across six regions, with 28,629 livestock lost and over 319 water points dried up, mainly in West Hararghe, North Gondar and parts of Tigray. headline: National Dialogue Commission closes: 394 recommendations, 400+ districts, ~4,000 at conference; no public implementation timetable (The Reporter, Oct 24)
status: posted by MG 10:44 PM Oct 25 (11pm slot, early)
caption:
Ethiopia news today: 394 recommendations from Ethiopia's National Dialogue.
The National Dialogue Commission said its mandate is fulfilled and was set to close on Oct 24, after consultations in 400+ districts and a national conference of about 4,000 participants. The Reporter notes no public timetable or lead institutions were given for putting the recommendations into practice. Records will go to Parliament and the national archives; House Speaker Ahmed Shide said the government will work to implement them.
Source: The Reporter, Oct 24, 2026.
#Ethiopia #EthiopiaNews #NationalDialogue #AddisAbaba #HornOfAfrica

headline: Transitional justice: draft laws ready for public review; Truth and Social Cohesion Commission, Special Prosecutor, Institutional Reform Commission proposed; CSO independence and Tigray participation questions (The Reporter, Oct 24)
caption:
Ethiopia news today: what is Ethiopia's transitional justice plan?
Justice Minister Hana Arayaselassie says draft laws are ready and will be published for public review in the coming days, followed by consultations in Addis Ababa, Dire Dawa and the regions. The drafts propose a Truth and Social Cohesion Commission, a Special Prosecutor's Office with a dedicated court bench, and an Institutional Reform Commission. Civil society groups asked about their independence and Tigray's participation; the ministry says it will only facilitate.
Source: The Reporter, Oct 24, 2026.
#Ethiopia #EthiopiaNews #TransitionalJustice #AddisAbaba #HumanRights

headline: Tigray local (woreda/kebele) elections underway: most Southern Tigray done except Raya Alamata/Alamata town; Eastern ongoing; paused in 2 Southeastern woredas; non-party, 6-month term; Redai Hailafom: positive start, stop restricting choice, faster IDP return (The Reporter, Oct 24)
caption:
Ethiopia news today: Tigray holds local elections.
District and village votes are underway across Tigray, The Reporter says. Most Southern Tigray districts have finished, except Raya Alamata and Alamata town; voting continues in Eastern Tigray and is paused in two Southeastern districts. Candidates run on personal merit, not party lists, for an initial six-month term. Caretaker official Redai Hailafom called it a positive start, said some activities limiting public choice must stop, and pledged faster return of displaced people.
Source: The Reporter, Oct 24, 2026.
#Ethiopia #Tigray #TigrayNews #Elections #EthiopiaNews

headline: Coffee governance study (Rift Valley Institute, 47 interviews, Kaffa/Bench-Sheko/Sheka): alleges politically connected traders shielded by selective enforcement, officials regulating and investing (unverified, no official response); smallholder debt, land loss, EU deforestation rule costs; $3bn exports 2025/26 (The Reporter, Oct 24)
caption:
Ethiopia news today: $3 billion in coffee exports in 2025/26. Who benefits?
A Rift Valley Institute study, based on 47 interviews in Kaffa, Bench-Sheko and Sheka zones, alleges that politically connected traders benefit from selective enforcement and that some officials both regulate the trade and invest in it. These claims are not independently verified, and the article includes no official response. The study also says smallholders depend on trader loans, some communities lost land to investment licences, and new EU traceability rules could add costs. It recommends a regional coffee governance council.
Source: The Reporter, Oct 24, 2026.
#Ethiopia #EthiopianCoffee #Coffee #Farmers #EthiopiaNews

headline: Russia–Africa summit (Moscow, Oct 28-29): Addis Ababa forum (UPEACE) weighs Ethiopia's gains; Ethiopia–Russia trade $191.2M in H1 2025, more than double (Russian ambassador); exports coffee/flowers/oilseeds/pulses, market access imbalance; judge summit on binding commitments (The Reporter, Oct 26)
caption:
Ethiopia news today: Russia–Africa summit, Ethiopia weighs the gains.
Ahead of the Russia–Africa summit in Moscow on Oct 28–29, a policy forum in Addis Ababa hosted by the University for Peace asked what Ethiopia would actually gain. Ethiopia–Russia trade reached $191.2 million in the first half of 2025, more than double a year earlier, according to Russia's ambassador. Ethiopia's exports are mainly coffee, flowers, oilseeds and pulses, and speakers called market access a core challenge. Participants said the summit should be judged on measurable, binding commitments.
Source: The Reporter, Oct 26, 2026.
#Ethiopia #EthiopiaNews #Russia #AfricaDiplomacy #AddisAbaba

headline: Arsi: EOTC Holy Synod reports lives lost in Merti and Shirka woredas (Oct 20, 24; unverified), asks for condemnation, civilian protection, justice, talks with officials; Oromia gov pledges to pursue perpetrators and blames rebel alliance, rebel-linked source blames regional gov, neither verified (Reuters; Al Jazeera, Oct 27). No death counts.
caption:
Ethiopia news today: Arsi, what are church leaders asking for?
The Ethiopian Orthodox Church's Holy Synod says lives were lost in Merti and Shirka districts of Arsi Zone, Oromia, on Oct 20 and 24 (not independently verified). It asks government bodies to condemn the violence publicly, protect civilians and bring those responsible to justice. Oromia's regional government pledged to pursue those responsible and blamed a rebel alliance; a rebel-linked source blamed the regional government. Neither claim is verified.
Source: Reuters; Al Jazeera, Oct 27, 2026.

headline: Northern Ethiopia humanitarian assessment (Oct 19, seen by Addis Standard): Raya Azebo only ~400 of 15,000+ cultivated ha show crop growth, ~10,000 ha unplanted after May rains failed; Zala Anbesa supplies scarce, prices rising; FEWS NET IPC 3 to Jan 2027; Wag Hamra cholera concern; 11,000-13,000 may remain displaced in Afar (unverified; Addis Standard, Oct 27). caption:
Ethiopia news today: 400 hectares of 15,000 planted showed crop growth in Raya Azebo, Tigray
That is what a humanitarian assessment dated Oct 19 and seen by Addis Standard reports; about 10,000 more hectares were not planted after rains failed in May. Few supplies were reaching Zala Anbesa as of Oct 15, and prices rose sharply. The assessment also flags a cholera concern in Wag Hamra, Amhara, and 11,000-13,000 people possibly still displaced in Afar. Not independently verified.

headline: Moyale update: Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (Oct 27) says ~40,000 from Ethiopia sought refuge in Moyale (15,000+ in eight shelters incl churches/schools, 20,000+ with relatives); urges food, water, shelter, sanitation, health incl maternal care; non-refoulement; Kenya-Ethiopia coordination; Kenya Red Cross had 14,000+ at weekend; figures differ, unverified (Anadolu; Citizen Digital, Oct 27). New development, not a translation of earlier Moyale videos
caption:
Ethiopia news today: about 40,000 from Ethiopia now in Moyale, Kenya
Kenya's National Commission on Human Rights said on Oct 27 that roughly 40,000 people have sought refuge in Moyale after leaving unrest in southern Ethiopia. More than 15,000 are in eight temporary shelters, including churches and schools; over 20,000 stay with relatives. The commission asks for food, water, shelter, sanitation and health care, and urges Kenya and Ethiopia to coordinate. Kenya Red Cross reported 14,000+ at the weekend; figures differ and are not independently verified.
Source: Anadolu Agency; Citizen Digital, Oct 27, 2026.
#Ethiopia #Moyale #Kenya #Displacement #EthiopiaNews

headline: Russia's FM Lavrov (Oct 28) says Moscow ready to host and facilitate Ethiopia–Eritrea meeting 'now, tomorrow, or the day after' if both sides interested; similar offer Oct 16 (Dep FM Alimov); neither government has publicly accepted, no Abiy–Isaias meeting confirmed; background: Red Sea access dispute (Addis Standard, Oct 28). New official statement; headline style to differ from 6am Abiy–Putin question video
caption:
Ethiopia Eritrea news: Russia offers to host Ethiopia–Eritrea talks
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said on Oct 28 that Moscow is ready to host and facilitate a meeting between Ethiopia and Eritrea if both sides are interested, "now, tomorrow, or the day after tomorrow." Neither government has publicly said it will accept, and no Abiy–Isaias meeting has been confirmed. Both leaders are in Russia for the Russia–Africa summit. Ties have been strained over Ethiopia's push for Red Sea access, which Eritrea sees as a threat to its sovereignty.
Source: Addis Standard, Oct 28, 2026.
#Ethiopia #Eritrea #Russia #RedSea #HornOfAfrica

caption:
Shire Tigray Ethiopia: 45 trucks of food aid reach Shire, Tigray.

OCHA says needs are outpacing relief and calls for urgent extra funding.

caption:
የአሜሪካ ኤምባሲ ለኢትዮጵያ አዲስ የደኅንነት ማስጠንቀቂያ አወጣ (ኢትዮጵያ የጉዞ ማስጠንቀቂያ)
የአሜሪካ ኤምባሲ አዲስ አበባ ኦክቶበር 28 ባወጣው መልዕክት ዜጎቹ ወደ አማራ፣ ትግራይና አፋር በምንም ምክንያት እንዳይጓዙ መክሯል። በአክሱምና በሽሬ አየር ማረፊያዎች በረራ አሁንም እንደተቋረጠ ገልጿል። ኤምባሲው ሁኔታው በማንኛውም ጊዜ ሊቀየር እንደሚችል አስጠንቅቆ፣ በሶሻል ሚዲያ የሚሰራጩ ሐሰተኛ መረጃዎችን ከበርካታ ታማኝ ምንጮች እንዲያረጋግጡ ጠይቋል።
ምንጭ፦ የአሜሪካ ኤምባሲ አዲስ አበባ፣ ኦክቶበር 28፣ 2026።
#Ethiopia #ኢትዮጵያ #Tigray #Amhara #TravelAlert

headline: Ethiopian passport: 90th in 2026 Global Passport Power Index, 17 visa-free, 33 visa on arrival, 5 AU states visa-free; reasons cited (Capital FM via AllAfrica, Oct 26; single source, unverified). Daily-life/travel angle, no conflict content.
caption:
Ethiopian passport visa-free travel: 17 destinations, a report says

Capital FM reports that the 2026 Global Passport Power Index ranks the Ethiopian passport 90th, with visa-free entry to 17 destinations and visa on arrival in 33. Five African Union states (Kenya, Benin, The Gambia, Rwanda and Togo) offer visa-free entry. The report cites economic conditions, security concerns and diplomatic relations. Single source, not independently verified.

Source: Capital FM, Oct 26, 2026.

#Ethiopia #EthiopianPassport #VisaFree #TravelNews #HornOfAfrica

headline: ICRC (Oct 20): supports 33 health facilities in Tigray, 32 in Amhara; supplies to hospitals in Shire, Maychew, Mehoni, Alamata, Mekelle Oct 13-16; relief kits 6,000 Tigray / 2,000 Amhara / 2,400 Afar; 161 evacuated Mekelle to Semera Sep 28; calls on all parties to protect civilians. Humanitarian angle, not previously covered
caption:
Ethiopia Red Cross news: ICRC backs hospitals in Tigray and Amhara.
The International Committee of the Red Cross says shortages of health care, water and food are a pressing concern in northern Ethiopia. It supports 33 health facilities in Tigray and 32 in Amhara, and sent supplies to hospitals in Shire, Maychew, Mehoni, Alamata and Mekelle on Oct 13-16. It also helped evacuate 161 people from Mekelle to Semera, and says safe passage needs agreement from all parties.
Source: ICRC, Oct 20, 2026.
#Ethiopia #Tigray #Amhara #RedCross #HumanitarianAid

headline: Kacha Digital Financial Service signs 5-year Mastercard deal to issue cards to own customers and eligible banks/MFIs/fintechs (The Reporter, Oct 27; single source). Economy/daily-life angle.
caption:
Kacha Mastercard deal Ethiopia: what is in it?
The Reporter says Kacha Digital Financial Service signed a five-year agreement with Mastercard to issue payment cards to its own customers. Kacha also plans card-issuing services for eligible banks, microfinance institutions and fintechs, subject to regulatory approvals. Fees, a launch date and partner names were not given.
Source: The Reporter Ethiopia, Oct 27, 2026.
#Ethiopia #Kacha #Mastercard #EthiopiaBusiness #DigitalPayments

headline: EHRCO statement (Oct 22, via The Reporter Oct 24): urges protection of civilians in Amhara, Gambella, Oromia, Benishangul-Gumuz; cites harm to civilians, abductions, displaced without aid (Gida Ayana); names state forces and armed groups; asks investigations, release of abducted workers, aid; no authority response noted. Single source, unverified.
caption:
Ethiopia human rights news: rights council urges protection of civilians in four regions.
The Ethiopian Human Rights Council (EHRCO) says civilians in Amhara, Gambella, Oromia and Benishangul-Gumuz need urgent protection. It reports people harmed, workers abducted and families displaced, and names both state security forces and armed groups. It asks for investigations, the release of abducted workers, and food, shelter and medical care. The Reporter says no federal or regional response was included. Not independently verified.
Source: The Reporter (EHRCO statement), Oct 24, 2026.
#Ethiopia #HumanRights #Amhara #Oromia #Gambella

headline: Shirka Woreda (Southeast/Arsi Zone, Oromia): residents tell Addis Standard 50+ detained after burying victims/helping wounded; some mourners incl. women held; grounds unclear; regional comms head blamed armed group, no comment on detentions (Addis Standard, Oct 28; single source, unverified). New development (detentions) vs Oct 27 Arsi church-leaders video; no counts of dead.
caption:
Shirka Oromia Ethiopia: more than 50 people reported detained, residents say.
Residents told Addis Standard that young people who buried the dead or helped the wounded were held, and that mourners were also detained. Grounds for the arrests are unclear. A regional official blamed an armed group for the violence but did not address the detentions. Not independently verified. Calls: protect civilians, investigate independently, respect due process.
Source: Addis Standard, Oct 28, 2026.
#Ethiopia #Oromia #Shirka #HumanRights #EthiopiaNews

headline: Amharic: Sudan officials (Khartoum presser Oct 28, via Sudan Tribune/Addis Standard Oct 29) accuse Ethiopia of involvement in drone attacks on power/fuel sites, say launched from Ethiopian territory incl. Bahir Dar; Ethiopia not reached for comment; unverified, single source.
caption:

አዲስ ስታንዳርድ ሱዳን ትሪቡንን ጠቅሶ እንደዘገበው፣ ባለሥልጣናቱ ኢትዮጵያ በሱዳን የኃይል ማመንጫና የነዳጅ ማከማቻዎች ላይ በደረሱ የድሮን ጥቃቶች ተሳትፎ አላት ይላሉ፤ የበረራ መረጃና የሳተላይት ምስል አቅርበናል ብለዋል። የኢትዮጵያ ባለሥልጣናት ወዲያውኑ አስተያየት ለመስጠት አልተገኙም። ክሱ በገለልተኛ አካል አልተረጋገጠም። ውይይትና ገለልተኛ ምርመራ ያስፈልጋል።

headline: Aid response for Ethiopians hosted in Kenya (UNICEF via UN News Oct 27): 36,600+ hosted, nutrition supplies, 4 water tanks, hygiene kits ~1,000 households; WFP/IOM/UNHCR join. New angle (aid arriving) vs Oct 28 Moyale UNHCR video.
caption:
Moyale Kenya Ethiopia: what help is reaching Ethiopians who fled to Kenya?
UNICEF says Kenyan authorities are leading a response plan for more than 36,600 Ethiopians who fled insecurity in the south. UNICEF reports delivering nutrition supplies to a local hospital, water tanks and hygiene kits for about 1,000 households. WFP, IOM and UNHCR have joined the response. Calls: protect people seeking safety and keep aid flowing.
Source: UN News (UNICEF), Oct 27, 2026.
#Ethiopia #Moyale #Kenya #HumanitarianAid #EthiopiaNews

headline: Background explainer: What is the Pretoria Agreement? (UN News Oct 10: 2022 accord; Guterres urges cessation of hostilities and return to dialogue; aid access; displacement, no verified figures). Fallback explainer: no fresh clean non-repeated story found.
caption:
Pretoria Agreement Ethiopia Tigray: what is it, and why does it matter now?
UN News describes the 2022 Pretoria Agreement as the accord that ended the civil war in Tigray. On Oct 10, UN Secretary-General Guterres urged all parties to stop hostilities and the signatories to return to dialogue under its framework. The UN says teams are working to get food and health care through, but hostilities are displacing people in Tigray, and verified figures are not yet available.
Source: UN News, Oct 10, 2026.
#Ethiopia #Tigray #PretoriaAgreement #HumanitarianAid #EthiopiaNews

headline: Tigray: ~3.9M need emergency food (Tigray DRMC Sept assessment, via Addis Standard commentary); IDP ration delays in Mekelle; ICRC supplies
caption:
Tigray food aid Ethiopia: about 3.9 million people need emergency food, a commentary says.
The Addis Standard commentary cites a September assessment by the Tigray Disaster Risk Management Commission; the figure is not independently verified. The author, citing one displaced woman in Mekelle, says food rations were often late. The ICRC says it delivered medical supplies across Tigray but insecurity threatens civilians' access to treatment, food and clean water. Calls: protect civilians and keep aid access open.
Source: Addis Standard (commentary) via allAfrica, Oct 30, 2026.
#Ethiopia #Tigray #Mekelle #HumanitarianAid #EthiopiaNews
